items.title: Department of Commerce extends RELIEF program timelines to support exporters facing geopolitical risks

It would provide 95% risk coverage to exporters who obtain ECGC cover for upcoming shipments to the specified regions for certain cargo types.

items.summary: India's tourism industry could face a shortage of around 11 million workers by 2035 as demand for trained professionals struggles to keep pace with expanding hotels and emerging tourism segments, according to a CBRE Research report. The report highlighted gaps in specialised skills, worker retention and training capacity, particularly in tier-II and tier-III cities.

items.summary: Nitin Gadkari defended the Centre's ethanol-blending programme at the Bihar Investor Summit 2026, rejecting claims that ethanol-blended petrol damages vehicles. He said millions of vehicles have been running on blended fuel since 2022 and highlighted the policy's potential to reduce fuel imports while creating additional income opportunities for farmers through ethanol production.

items.title: Passenger accidentally touches emergency door of flight at Hyderabad airport; deboarded
items.summary: A 35-year-old passenger was deboarded from a flight at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad. The incident occurred as the flight was preparing for take-off to Kadapa on Thursday. While adjusting his seat, the passenger unintentionally touched the emergency exit door handle, activating the sensor alarm. The airline staff then deboarded him, and police were contacted to investigate the matter.

items.title: Suzuki asks India suppliers to move to 6-day, 20-hour operations by Sept 2027, sources say
items.summary: Suzuki Motor has requested Indian suppliers to implement a maintenance break for one day each week. This strategy aims to improve quality and prevent unscheduled production stoppages as output is expanded. Suppliers must sign declarations confirming that production lines will not operate continuously seven days a week. Amid rising demand in the domestic market, the company plans to boost car production to meet future targets.

items.summary: Japanese rubber futures saw a minor decline amid a slight pullback in Tokyo equities, yet they continue to show prospects for growth. The Osaka Exchange's rubber contract dropped due to concerns over interest rates and geopolitical instability. With natural rubber production declining alongside consumption, the market faces ongoing supply challenges.

The fundraising requires shareholder approval; institutional investors will receive QIP shares while promoter warrants could help maintain Bajaj Finserv’s stake and limit dilution.

items.title: FCNR inflows cushion rupee, BoP; FII flows crucial for sustained external stability: Report
items.summary: Foreign currency non-resident inflows have significantly bolstered rupee stability and India's balance of payments. However, the current support from these inflows may not suffice for long-term external stability. Foreign institutional investor flows are crucial for maintaining economic balance as the support from FCNR is absorbed. India's goods deficit has reached a decade-high despite continuous support from services exports and remittances.

items.title: APSEZ operational performance update shows growth in cargo and logistics performance
items.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd reported that cargo handling rose in September 2026. The company handled 46 million metric tonnes, marking an 11% increase over the previous year. Container cargo contributed to this growth with a 15% year-on-year rise. However, logistics rail volume experienced a decrease in the first half of FY27. This was despite a 3% increase in September for rail volumes.

Existing trade agreements with the UK and Australia are also under review for their implementation and effectiveness.

Operational control changed from Thursday, while administrative and financial separation is expected to take another 30 to 45 days. Meanwhile, railway users have raised concerns over changes to the Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat service.

items.summary: India's economic growth is projected to slow to 5.5-6% in the second half of 2026-27. This slowdown follows a robust growth of 7-7.5% in the first half of the financial year. Combined capital expenditure growth is expected to moderate significantly from 13.2% to around 4% in the latter months. Additionally, the central government's capital expenditure growth will weaken due to a declining fiscal position.

items.summary: The yield on the 10-year Treasury note has surged past its 2007 high, now sitting at 5.34%. At the same time, 30-year US bonds have hit a 24-year peak this week. The rise in global sovereign debt is primarily driven by escalating oil prices amid the ongoing Middle Eastern conflict. Investors are now bracing for potentially further interest rate hikes from central banks.

items.summary: Indian equity markets faced significant pressure as US bond yields surged, leading to a record selloff. Foreign investors continued to withdraw their investments amidst rising crude oil prices, negatively impacting the rupee's value. Analysts suggest selective stock opportunities may arise despite challenging macroeconomic conditions.

With 22 projects planned, the anticipated gross development value ranges from ₹17,500 to ₹18,000 crore. Furthermore, collections have surged year-over-year, suggesting a bright growth trajectory for the current fiscal year.

Washington is also considering a diesel export ban, putting pressure on France and Germany to tap stockpiles. US diesel prices have climbed more than 70% since the war began, reaching $6.39 a gallon.
